• Nephrology Social Worker: The
primary role of the social worker is
to assist the CKD patient and im-
mediate family in their adjustment
to the patient’s chronic illness. This
involves a psychosocial assessment,
provision of emotional support, and 
educational reinforcement. The
social worker is a valuable resource
for information pertaining to the
patient’s behavior, history, and 
functioning that may inﬂ uence the 
patient’s care and course of treat-
ment.
• Renal Dietitian: The dietitian is
primarily responsible for nutritional
assessment and nutrition therapy. 
Nutrition therapy includes devel-
oping a plan for nutritional man-
agement, counseling the patient,
monitoring nutrient intake, and
providing educational activities and
ongoing reinforcement to maximize
dietary adherence. One aspect of
assessment is to review monthly 
laboratory tests and nutrition-
related parameters and to counsel
the patient appropriately. Labora-
tory indicators relating to bone and
mineral disorders, anemia, and ad-
equacy of dialysis are also reviewed,
and appropriate recommendations
are made to the nephrologist.
In some cases, the role of the RD in a
dialysis facility is expanded beyond the
traditional role outlined here. Some
renal dietitians monitor protocols and
make recommendations on anemia and
bone and mineral disorder therapies. In
some instances, they are instrumental
in leading continuous quality improve-
ment efforts.
